option_relations.rationale: The description of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion with enhancement and signal-intensity characteristics identical to those of extraocular muscle suggests an accessory extraocular muscle.
Cranial nerve palsy is not directly related to the orbital linear soft-tissue lesion described.
Schwannoma is not directly related to the orbital linear soft-tissue lesion described, which has characteristics of extraocular muscle.
Thyroid eye disease could be considered in the differential diagnosis, but the specific characteristics of the lesion do not directly suggest this condition.
Orbital mass is a broader category that could encompass the described lesion, but it is not specific enough given the details provided.
Intracranial mass lesion is not directly related to the orbital linear soft-tissue lesion described.
Congenital syndromes like Duane Retraction Syndrome could be considered, given the long-standing diplopia and specific characteristics of the lesion.
None is not applicable as there are potential diagnoses related to the described condition.
